newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-GDRs rise on new gov't, Bombay climb.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-GDRs rise on new gov't, Bombay climb.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts posted steady gains on Monday, following the resolution of the country's political crisis and a rise in Bombay stocks, dealers said.
They said news that Inder Kumar Gujral had been sworn in as India's new prime minister had driven gains in Indian shares and aided further GDR strength.
The 77-year-old Gujral retained the cabinet of his predecessor, H.D. Deve Gowda, except for Finance Minister P. Chidambaram and four other departing ministers.
Traders said the 1997/8 budget was now expected to be passed without significant changes.

But they said GDR price gains had been capped as they had risen in anticipation of the news when Indian stock markets were closed on Friday. As a result GDR premiums to local stocks had risen sharply.
Reliance added 62 cents to $19.00/20.00 following strong gains in India ahead of annual results due on Tuesday.
State Bank of India picked up 46 cents to $23.15/24.15 and VSNL made 70 cents to $20.20/21.20.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.37 points, or 1.72 percent, up at 81.28 following Friday's 2.96 percent gains. The premium over the local market at 23.35 percent from 24.62 percent on Friday.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 0.58 points to 126.08 in line with a local market rebound, representing a discount to the local market to 3.74 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.12 points, or 0.19 percent, up at 64.66, a premium of 33.16 percent over the local market.
